title: Alcort D/0004: Ferdinand I (Prague) to Pedro Lasso de Castilla and Gamiz, cipher in most part, deciphered in the margins (DARA i=764847)
correspondents: Ferdinand I (Prague) -> Pedro Lasso de Castilla and Gamiz
shelfmark: Fundacion Hospital de Benasque, Fundacion Alcort, ES/FHB - CD/ALCORT/D/0004
folio_note: At least three pages (page 3: 499 cipher tokens; page 2: about 1,000 signs). DARA: 'Documento cifrado en su mayor parte, y descifrado posteriormente en los margenes'. The decipherment of the time is on the sheet.
status: Online on DARA (images, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). The marginal decipherment of the time is the crib for a key. Two pre-registered tests of the key sheet Alcort D/0042 against this letter, both reported as failed at their bar (Brice Dudout, with Claude, 18 Nov 2026, issue #779): page 1 letter accuracy 0.547 against 0.344 for the best of 200 shuffled keys; page 3 0.812 against 0.442 (bar 0.85 missed by 0.038). Pages 1 and 3 are spent as test portions; page 2 is untouched. No target folder, no reading.
why: The letter has its own contemporary decipherment, so a key can be rebuilt from adjacent plaintext and tested on a held-out page. D/0042 (a homophonic alphabet with syllabic code words, names of Charles V's circle of c. 1547-1553) is a candidate key for it; its decode already reads as Spanish in places and reproduces the gloss on page 3 ("y tanto sera mayor ... ni la calidad del negocio lo sufre"), but it has not passed a test at the project's bar.
score_note: Scored from Brice Dudout's report on issue #779 (two tests, 18 Nov 2026); the DARA images were not re-read by the project
verify: Rebuild the key from the margin decipherment on page 2, freeze it and its sign identifications with a hash before any scoring (S01 and S17 are not told apart in the letter, hooked n, beta and 66 are separators or nulls: post hoc, not counted), transcribe in two blind passes, and report the result whichever way it goes. A pass validates that corrected version, not the 0.812. Compare with the imperial cipher of gonzaga1549, vargas1552 and the Simancas sheet: D/0042 is a different table (Papa = Bam against pollo).
